title: Helion Delta POC: budget-aligned throughput & benchmarks
summary: Discovery / POC scoping call focused on unit economics and benchmark plan. Helion Delta wants a 3-week pilot to validate per-token costs, latency SLOs, and throughput under a mixed workload. Agreement on dataset sample, success criteria (p50/p90 latency, cost per 1M tokens), and a tentative runbook: baseline->bench->opt. Action items include Redwood sending cost sensitivity sheet and benchmark template; Helion to provide representative request traces and a staging dataset.
topics: Benchmark types and metrics (p50/p90 latency, tokens/sec, cost/M tokens)
action_items: Maya Carter: Send cost sensitivity workbook (per-token scenarios + caching/batching assumptions) by 2026-07-13
Arun Patel: Share 10k sample request traces (anonymized) and current token distribution by 2026-07-14
Noah Singh: Prepare benchmark harness template and suggested test script (latency/throughput/50/90) by 2026-07-15
Helion Delta Team: Provision staging VPC access or sample dataset with ingest instructions by 2026-07-16
next_steps: Redwood to email pilot statement of work and price buckets for hosted vs dedicated options
Schedule 30-min kickoff to align on traces and dataset (target 2026-07-17)
Run baseline 2-day smoke bench once dataset is ingested
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-11
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Noah (SE), Arun (Helion), Lena (Platform), Samir (SRE), Priya (Product)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining, uh, we'll go for about an hour. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on this. Noah, our solutions engineer, will handle the bench specifics. Can y'all quickly intro?
[00:18] Arun: Hi I'm Arun, Head of ML at Helion. We're looking to scope a POC to understand the real unit economics for inference for our customer-facing summarization feature.
[00:27] Lena: Lena here — platform, I'll do the staging infra.
[00:32] Samir: Samir, SRE, mainly concerned about p95 latency and cost peaks.
[00:36] Priya: Priya, product, success criteria and timelines from the PM side.
[00:41] Noah: Great, quick agenda: baseline workload, sample traces, metrics and success criteria, bench plan and timeline, then deliverables.

[01:05] Arun: High level: we have ~120k requests/day today for the summarization API, average prompt ~140 tokens, avg completion ~90 tokens. Peak bursts up to 1.2k QPS for a minute. Our budget target for the pilot is to demonstrate we can hit approx $0.02 per user monthly — which translates into per-token limits but we wanted Redwood to help us model it.
[01:34] Maya: Okay that's helpful. A few quick clarifying q's — is the 120k steady or includes spikes? and do you store user prompts? any PII concerns?
[01:45] Arun: Mix — steady base 40k/day, peaks are usage-driven. We do redact PII but there is residual metadata. We need SOC2 controls and KMS in private deployments, but the POC can run on hosted if we mask traces.

[02:10] Noah: Great. On the cost side we typically model per-token compute + infra amortized GPU time + storage + networking. For your workload with avg request 230 tokens (prompt+response), baseline unoptimized per-token estimate on our hosted Redis-like runner for a mid-sized open model is about $6e-5 per token — so roughly $60 per 1M tokens. With batching and prefix caching we often see 30–60% reductions depending on reuse.
[02:42] Priya: Wait can you translate that to our numbers? 120k requests/day * 230 tokens = 27.6M tokens/day; at $60/M that's about $1,656/day or ~$50k/month — that's above our target.
[03:01] Maya: Exactly, so the POC will show delta across knobs. If prefix caching reduces tokens by 40% for repetitively similar prompts you get down to ~16.5M tokens/day and cost ~990/day. Also batching reduces per-token GPU overhead — in some cases by another 20%. Quantization + int8 can shave 15–25% on GPU utilization and thus unit cost. So we need to validate on your traces how much repetition exists.
[03:32] Samir: For latency SLOs we need p50 < 200ms and p90 < 700ms — that's our internal bar. Can Redwood meet that with batching? We're worried batching increases p90.
[03:44] Noah: Right, batching is a tradeoff. Continuous batching with dynamic deadlines can keep p50 nice while keeping p90 bounded; we can also do hybrid routing — small requests hit low-latency pool, larger or batchable requests go to a throughput pool. During the POC we'll test strict SLOs: scenario A — low-latency pool only, scenario B — mixed with batching and fallback.

[04:12] Arun: What about dedicated capacity vs hosted? Helm-ing private on prem is expensive for us — but we need to compare.
[04:20] Maya: Hosted is fastest to iterate; dedicated gives predictable unit economics when you have sustained throughput because you amortize GPU cost. For your 27M tokens/day sustained, dedicated with reserved capacity could be more economical if you commit, but only if utilization is high. We'll run a cost sensitivity sheet with break-even utilization percentages.

[04:46] Priya: For the POC success criteria, we propose: 1) Show per-token cost <= $0.00004 after optimizations OR show path to it with clear steps; 2) Demonstrate p50/p90 targets for representative traffic; 3) Throughput target: sustain 1.2k QPS burst for at least 1 minute without >5% error rate.
[05:05] Maya: Sounds good. We'll formalize these as the POC success criteria. We'll also instrument token-level billing and tracing so you can see where tokens are saved from caching.

[05:20] Noah: For the benchmark harness: we ask for a 10k sample of real requests with token counts and a simple scoring rubric — measure p50/p90 latencies, tail latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, and cost per 1M tokens normalized. We'll run three phases: baseline (no caching, default batch=1), mid (batching tuned, quantized model), and optimized (prefix/KV caching + batching + routing rules).

[06:02] Lena: On infra, we can provide a staging VPC and temporary credentials. We want to validate SSO and KMS later but for the POC we can mask data.
[06:10] Noah: Perfect. We'll give a bench harness that runs locally or in your staging, collects perf and cost counters, and posts aggregated results.

[07:00] Arun: A couple of specifics — our prompt distribution: 60% short (<100 tokens), 30% medium (100–300), 10% long (>300). What batch sizes do you find effective for mixed workload?
[07:16] Noah: For those proportions, dynamic batching with an upper batch cap of 8 for short and 4 for medium tends to hit the sweet spot; long ones we route individually or in small batch sizes because they blow up KV cache. We'll include recommended knobs.

[07:40] Samir: On caching — you mentioned prefix and KV cache. Can you explain expected savings and consistency tradeoffs?
[07:49] Maya: Prefix caching stores common prompt/response prefixes reducing decoded tokens; KV cache is per-request state for autoregressive reuse — it's best when prompts share context windows. Savings depend on reuse: for chatty repeated prompts we often see 30–60% token reduction; for one-off prompts it's minimal. There's also a freshness tradeoff — caching invalidation policies required.

[08:20] Priya: From a product POV we need deterministic quality — quantization sometimes affects output. How do you guard for quality regressions?
[08:29] Noah: We run evals on a held-out prompt set with automatic metrics (BLEU/ROUGE-ish, embedding similarity) plus human spot checks. For the POC we'll tie quality regression alerts to the eval set and provide thresholds. If quantization degrades quality beyond agreed tolerance we'll back off.

[09:05] Arun: Can you walk through a quick cost sensitivity example live?
[09:09] Maya: Sure — baseline: 27.6M tokens/day * $60/1M = $1,656/day. With prefix caching 40%: tokens -> 16.56M/day -> $994/day. With batching + quantization saves another ~35% on compute -> effective tokens-day-equivalent ~10.76M -> $646/day. Monthly (30-day) range: $19k (optimized) to $50k (baseline). We'll include the workbook so you can change assumptions.

[09:50] Lena: That delta is huge — good to get numbers exactly from our traces.

[10:02] Noah: We'll also model tail-cost from retries, network egress, and cold-starts. Cold-start GPU spin-up only affects ephemeral scaling in hosted; in dedicated we can keep warm pools to reduce that cost at the expense of higher baseline.

[10:30] Arun: For benchmarks, do you run on our staging VPC or Redwood-hosted?
[10:34] Maya: Either. Redwood-hosted is faster to start and we can do a synthetic run. But for accurate networking and real infra constraints, running the bench harness in your staging VPC is best. We'll provide a Dockerized harness.

[11:00] Priya: Timeline?
[11:02] Maya: We propose a 3-week POC: Week 0 (2 business days) align on traces and infra; Week 1 run baseline + smoke tests; Week 2 run full benchmark across scenarios (3–4 runs to get stable p90); Week 3 optimizations (caching, batching, quantize) and final report + review.
[11:20] Arun: Sounds reasonable. What is the minimal Redwood time commitment?
[11:24] Maya: AE + SE time: kickoff + 3 checkpoints ~ 6–8 hours total, plus SE-run bench orchestration ~ 1.5 days of labor. We'll include hours in the SOW.

[11:50] Samir: Regarding security: we need SOC2 and audit logs and KMS integration if we go dedicated. Can you produce an HLD?
[11:58] Noah: Yes, we'll attach security pack and private deployment checklist. For POC we can do masked traces and provide an RA for KMS integration later.

[12:18] Priya: Any pitfalls you've seen with similar customers?
[12:22] Maya: Biggest surprises are often around tokenization mismatches and sample bias — customers send partially preprocessed inputs which inflate token counts. Also optimistic caching assumptions fail if prompts are too unique. We'll validate with your real traces.

[12:40] Arun: Quick question on metrics: in your dashboard do you show token-level cost attribution by customer route?
[12:46] Noah: Yes, Redwood Console has per-route token/time breakdown, cost attribution, and you can tie it to API keys or routes. We'll enable a dashboard for the POC.

[13:05] Maya: Ok let's capture decisions: Helion will send a 10k sample trace; Redwood will send bench harness, cost workbook, and SOW. Target kickoff next Friday.
[13:18] Priya: Agreed. Also want a quick mock report showing expected monthly cost ranges given three scenarios (baseline, mid, optimized).

[13:30] Arun: Any competitor reasons — we are also talking to Vertex and Anthropic for similar pilots. Key decider is unit cost predictability and integration effort.
[13:40] Maya: Understood. We'll highlight break-even analysis and required infra changes.

[14:02] Noah: A couple of nitty-gritty on bench config: we suggest 90th percentile sampling window of 5 minutes for p90 to capture bursts; use 95th for error rate spikes. For tokens/sec we report both aggregated and per-model. We'll log GPU-utilization via nvidia-smi or telemetry if on-prem.

[14:45] Samir: For your suggested batch cap numbers, please include a fallback policy that if latency exceeds SLO we drop batch and route to low-latency pool.
[14:52] Noah: Yep, that will be in the runbook.

[15:12] Lena: We'll provide staging creds — do you need IAM roles or ephemeral tokens?
[15:16] Maya: Ephemeral tokens are fine; we'll give exact permissions in the onboarding doc.

[15:35] Priya: For the benchmark acceptance, we'll accept if two runs for optimized scenario show p50/p90 within targets and cost is within +/- 10% of modeled optimized case.

[15:45] Maya: Sounds fair. Anything else?
[15:48] Arun: No, that's it from me.

[16:00] Maya: Great — recap of action items and next steps we'll email right after. Thanks everyone.

[57:40] Call ended.

Notes on transcription: occasional words garbled (e.g., nvidia-smi transcribed as nvidi a smi in earlier auto transcripts), timestamps approximate.
notes: Bench harness will be Dockerized and include a results JSON schema
Redwood to include quantization/throughput tradeoff examples for model families in the workbook
Helion to anonymize traces to remove PII before upload
